topics.name: Counting
intro: How many things there are, without listing them.
Comes before graphs: counting edges reuses the range sum.
Rows build from one range sum to the three rules.

picks.title: Staircase sums, drawn (sample)
picks.visuals: Two staircases fitted into a rectangle.
picks.why: Shows the pairing trick as a picture before any algebra.
picks.thread: Starts the topic: what a range sum is; sets up the closed form the lecture uses.
differs: Writes the sum with i from 0, where the notes start at 1.
picks.tested: Compute a range sum in closed form and show the pairing.

also.lead: From a cut video on the same trick:
items: An odd count leaves one middle term.

picks.title: Lecture 3, the range sum
picks.thread: Picks up the pairing from row 1 in the course's notation; sets up the rules.
picks.tested: Same as row 1, in the course's notation.

picks.title: A friend's whiteboard take (sample)
picks.why: Short, and the board stays readable.
picks.thread: A second pass on the same picture, faster.
differs: Calls the closed form a formula without deriving it.
picks.tested: Recognize the closed form on sight.

picks.thread: No video separates the three rules the way the notes do.

explain.label: Rule
explain.text: Sum for either-or, product for one-then-another, subtract the overlap.

explain.label: Answer form
explain.text: The rule named, then the count.

topics.name: Graphs
intro: Differs from counting: here the object is the structure, not the number.

picks.title: Lecture 3, nodes and edges
picks.why: The lecture's definitions, word for word.
picks.thread: Starts the topic with the definitions.
differs: Draws edges as arrows before saying the graph is directed.
picks.tested: Define a graph and count its edges.

picks.title: Walking a graph, step by step (sample)
picks.why: Traces each walk one edge at a time.
picks.thread: Builds on the edges from the row before.
differs: Uses a dot for a node where the notes use a circle.
picks.tested: Trace a walk and give its length.
